speaker: The Chairman
text: Head I, Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF).

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Singapore's success, resilience and unity are built on the foundation of a strong social compact, which has been built up by generations over the years.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Our social compact is anchored in the strong partnership between individuals and families, the community and the Government.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: It is the shared understanding of the various roles and responsibilities that different stakeholders play.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In this compact, instead of an exercise of raw might and power, where the strong prosper and the weak perish, we have a society where we all agree on a set of rules, that distributes resources and ensures opportunities in ways we all think are fair and just.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: As Singapore develops, both economically and politically, our language has become more alive with contests of values, and consensus about public goals is harder to achieve.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Both developments are, to me at least, great virtues of a small and vulnerable state like Singapore.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have nothing but good ideas, and these can only come through vigorous, honest debate and a commitment to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I stress "honest" because, often, the policy problems that we deal with are highly complex and require not just a deep recollection of history, but also a willingness to invest time, mental and emotional energy into a topic.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: At the same time, it is important for those of us who do want to, or have a duty to, take part in debates on public policy issues, to be willing to make commitments to honest, high integrity debates and to work for the good of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: I had said in my main Budget speech that this Budget breaks away from the past and, hence, gives a new shape to our social compact.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have a population that is ageing, that is facing many social pressures in a world that is increasingly uncertain.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We have become more generous, in giving subsidies, employment and other forms of welfare.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: In fact, in terms of the depth and reach of social spending, "welfare" should not be a dirty word.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: At the same time, for areas, such as preventive health, which we just debated, the Government has shifted to a more generous "subsidies-for-all" regime, as can be seen in the vaccination programme.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The Government also strives to provide subsidies in a way to achieve welfare without eroding the work ethic.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: That is the first element of our social compact – that the most go to the people who have the least, so that their lives would be free from precariousness and be rooted in dignity.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But these two countries are also among the most highly-taxed populations.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Singapore tries to keep both Government expenditure and taxes low by targeted subsidies and a progressive tax regime.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: The third element of our social compact speaks about opportunities – in our investments in innovation, employability and progress for every worker.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: As we continue to build the society that Singaporeans want to see, we can take heart that we are moving forward from a strong foundation.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: From the Forward Singapore (ForwardSG) conversations that have been ongoing for some time, I would like to ask the Minister to share what he feels are the critical pillars that need more attention to strengthen our social compact going forward.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Chairman, when I was in my 20s, my strong sense of social justice caused me to constantly question how much more welfare our Government can, and should provide for the less privileged among us.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In my 50s now, and after spending about 16 years with the social service sector and another four years with the primary and community healthcare sector through my former job in the Public Service, I have a much deeper appreciation of what it takes to uplift the lives of those amongst us who need more support in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Challenging economic times can weaken the social fabric and inequalities, if left unchecked, can widen income gaps.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Social mobility may slow if students from less financially able and stable families have lesser opportunities than their peers to optimise their potential.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: These are social trends that we are familiar with and there is much learning we can glean from developed countries with longer history and development, like the US, Europe and the Scandinavian countries.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, I wonder if our unique history, our nation-building philosophy that has seen us leapfrog from Third-World to First-World in one generation and our multiracial and multicultural society may yield us a context that requires us to delve deeper and consider social interventions and approaches that have and will work better for Singaporeans in the years ahead.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In this aspect, I would like to ask two questions.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Mr Chairman, families are the bedrock of our society and are often our first lines of support.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Have the efforts of programmes, such as Families for Life (FFL), been effective?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Beyond strengthening families, we also need to pay attention to marriages that are at risk of falling apart.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In 2021, there was a sharp spike in divorce applications filed, in part, due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Will we see a continued upward trend in divorce cases?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: I certainly hope that this does not happen, as the impact on the individuals and the children, if any, can be significant.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: As a Catholic, I went through a marriage preparation programme conducted by the Church to help me and my then wife-to-be understand the challenges of married life.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The programme equipped us with conflict management tools and how we can build a lasting relationship.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: We celebrated our Silver Jubilee just two weeks ago.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: One initiative that I find heartwarming is the Golden Jubilee Celebration, an annual event started in 2018 to honour couples who have been married for 50 years.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: It is a wonderful way to reaffirm a couple's love and commitment to their marriage.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, though our policies aim to encourage parenthood within marriage, penalising unwed single mothers will invariably penalise the children as well.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: These unwed single mothers are usually already the sole breadwinner and the caregiver of the family.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Having these policies would further exacerbate unequal access and reduce the social mobility of these children.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: It was found that it is likely that quite a number may be working in part-time jobs or only for a few months of the year, contributing to their lower monthly income.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: This may be because they are forced to take part-time jobs, which do not pay as well, as they juggle their caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: As they may have financial struggles as well, could we also consider granting them the Baby Bonus cash gift?

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Chairman, Sir, I would like to ask MSF how we can accelerate the adoption of the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA).

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: More Singaporeans, especially seniors, need to do up their LPAs so that they can get their wishes better respected, should they lose mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: Our society will have to pay a high price if there is no widespread adoption of LPAs.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: And as LPAs becomes more prevalent, there is also a chance of abuse by a small number of donees.

speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
text: The People's Action Party (PAP) senior group closely monitor these issues, given their importance.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: At Singapore's current stage of development, no child should fear going hungry or missing out on school, especially preschool.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Since 2016, the KidSTART programme led by the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) has been in place to help children from low-income families to have a good start in life.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Under KidSTART, ECDA provides services for families and monitors the developmental progress of children from birth onwards.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Can the Minister tell us if this number is the anticipated number at steady state, or are there more children who have not yet accessed these resources?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: If so, what is MSF going to do to ensure better outreach?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Second, is the current level of support adequate for these families?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Third, given that it is already seven years since the start of the programme, can the Minister provide some data to show how children under this programme has fared since 2016?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Chairman, last year, the ForwardSG dialogue was held to provide a platform for social service practitioners to voice their concerns.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: In the dialogue, one social service practitioner underscored how children from less advantaged backgrounds face hurdles to success, such as low morale from not performing as well as their peers.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Notably, he mentioned, "We always observe that people from disadvantaged backgrounds feel discouraged.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: But, sometimes, they just find it too difficult." In view of this practitioner's account, it is evident that preschoolers from lower-income families face more challenges in getting a good start in life.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Furthermore, it was also noted that there is growing evidence to show that children who attend preschool early require lesser intervention from learning support programmes, in juxtaposition to children who do not attend preschools, perhaps due to financial hardship.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: In view of this, could MSF share its existing efforts to provide greater support for children from lower-income families?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Leon Perera, you have three cuts, please.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, the trampoline is used to talk about helping individuals bounce back.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Safety nets are equally important but, today, I will make proposals to improve the trampoline.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The cost of healthy eating is a key reason why we say it is expensive to be poor.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Would the Government consider offering vouchers programmed to help parents buy healthier foods, like whole fruits and vegetables, to help children start off on the right foot?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: For schools, MoneySENSE co-funds vendor talks and workshops covering at least one of three tiers: basic money management, financial planning and investment know-how.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Since schools infuse financial literacy in Character and Citizenship Education and Food and Consumer Education curricula, could they dovetail the three MoneySENSE tiers into existing curricula to avoid repetition while ensuring good coverage of topics?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, I want to draw attention to three possibly underserved groups in our social service landscape.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: In most cases, NSFs need to depend on their family, at least in terms of housing and are unlikely to be able to save anything without this support.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Has the Ministry of Defence (MINDEF) or other Government bodies studied whether these allowances have resulted in increased poverty within this group, for those from poorer families?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My colleague, Mr Gerald Giam, raised a related issue recently.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Grant quantums are low and are not meant to replace paid work.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Again, there is a dearth of research here.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I have heard from ex-inmates that work programmes pay up to around $1,000 monthly.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Has the Government studied the financial impact of incarceration and whether this, in turn, has impacts on poverty and recidivism?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Mr Chairman, our Family Service Centres (FSCs) and Social Service Offices (SSOs) are intended to be the core nodes for social support.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Our social workers are best placed to understand and respond to residents' needs.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Social workers help point residents to more specific assistance schemes, such as those for students.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Such professional training should be brought to bear on financial assistance decisions, as opposed to taking a rigid schemes administration approach.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Also, would the Ministry consider centralising under SSO social workers all financial assistance schemes that are not sector-specific?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: This includes Community Development Council (CDC) cash assistance.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Currently, I understand that residents have to approach both the FSC social worker and the CDC, going through means testing twice.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: CDC takes two to three weeks for COVID-19 grants and financial assistance.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Leon Perera, can you please wrap up?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I chair the ComLink alliances in two ComLink towns – Jalan Besar and Ang Mo Kio.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: There are three critical success factors needed for ComLink to be effective.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And I seek the MSF's support to make it happen.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Many like-minded parties are still unclear about how all the many helping hands for families in public rental housing are connected.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: These integrators have to be able to pull in other agency representatives in the ComLink Workgroup Alliance for meetings and actions.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: I have the privilege of working with SSO general managers and FSCs' social workers who play this role really well; but they are not easily available.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Are all alliance partners equally committed or is ComLink seen as just an MSF-driven project?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: So, for ComLink to be successful, there must be clarity, competence and commitment.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Graduated beneficiaries can relate well to families in rental housing as they have experienced similar challenges before.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: They can be effective in building trust and rapport, which are critical for effective social support.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: At the same time, they can provide useful and honest feedback from the bridging perspective of both the user and intervener, to help address implementation gaps which sometimes officers from the public agencies may not be cognisant of.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Receiving supplementary part-time income from this programme will also help their financial adequacy and social mobility.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: Paying it forward with their time and empathy to others also enhances their self-esteem and dignity.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan (Nee Soon)
text: These can make them positive role models to give ComLink families the hope and encouragement they need to overcome their adversities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: SSOs support the less fortunate and less able in our society with the Community Care Endowment Fund or ComCare payouts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: During my Meet-the-People Sessions, I have occasionally encountered residents who had shared with me about their reluctance to pursue ComCare assistance because they find that the approval process is intrusive, onerous or demeaning.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: SSO officers often require a careful and complete accounting of a household's income and expenses, and offers strong indications of what they regard as reasonable or not.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: At some level, this is fair and expected.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: ComCare are public monies and the Government has to be responsible with the disbursement of such funds.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But, on the other, it is important to allow the needy to retain their dignity, even as they seek financial assistance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: There is one way that we can potentially soften the intrusiveness of this process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: A significant share of assistance rendered is in the form of regular bills with public and semi-public agencies, such as rental, utilities and service and conservancy charges (S&CC).

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Could these be obtained directly from these entities rather than provided by the resident?

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: I understand that this would mean potentially additional costs, at least at the outset, in terms of setting up informational exchange systems.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But once established, the automation will reduce the need for additional verification or data entry.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: This is the added advantage that the system could be tuned to flag extraordinary increases or decreases, should these occur to better target assistance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: There is yet another strategy that we can also deploy to reduce the need for documentary scrutiny.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: We can deploy conditional cash transfers, or CCTs, in exchange for supplementary educational expenditures, such as tuition or fees and equipment spending for co-curricular activities, or CCAs.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Such support will enable low-income children who would otherwise be unable to pursue such opportunities, which are increasingly becoming de rigueur in a holistic education in Singapore.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Of course, disbursements will be conditional on their continued participation in these activities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: CCTs have been successful deployed in many advanced and developing countries settings for the purposes of social protection, especially in terms of improving outcomes for school-going children.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: CCTs are also not alien in the local context.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In this regard, the Straits Times School Pocket Money Fund supports around 12,000 beneficiaries, providing cash in exchange for school assistance.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Research suggests that the Straits Times School Pocket Money Fund has achieved is educational goals.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: But such beneficiaries are likely to be a fraction of those of school-going age who are in need of financial help, the support is of a limited duration and the grant amounts are also relatively small.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Mr Chairman, I believe that SSOs already apply some conditionality for ComCare payouts, requiring households that receive financial support ensure that their children attend school.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: A CCT explicitly for ComCare targeted towards supplementary educational expenditures will fill a gap in our educational support for low-income households while keeping children as well as their parents accountable.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: As a House, we have each year approved increased spending on early childhood.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: As a result, preschool affordability and quality has improved, in particular for children aged three to six.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But what about those younger than three years old?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: To nurture and develop children in their early years, families would need to consider all care options available to them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Centre-based care may not be the best solution for all families, if parents and other family members are able to provide familial care for the very young.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: What is the Ministry doing to assure parents that there will be accessible support in their children's early years?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: The Government had earlier said that ECDA will be reviewing the Early Years Development Framework (EYDF) for educators of children aged three and below and that this will include new areas, such as the learning of mother tongue languages and creating an inclusive classroom environment.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Can the Minister update us on the outcome of this review?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Mr Chairman, in my Budget debate speech last week, I spoke about the importance of supporting our young families amidst the rise in cost of living.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Having affordable preschool is an important aspect of such support.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: My question is, for estates where there are preschools not run by the AOP and partner operator centres and young families have no choice but to send their infants and preschoolers to these centres because of distance or shortage of places, can these subsidies be made portable for them?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I would argue that this derived average of about $150 a month is not enough in most cases for a core welfare scheme.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Similarly, the Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) provides about $300 in cash per month.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: For someone earning a little over $1,000 or less, these schemes do defray expenses, but assessed against academic research on minimum income standards, as I alluded to in last year's Budget debate, this is woefully inadequate for care protection and bouncing back.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Would MSF at least trial higher ComCare amounts to test the effect on real outcomes, including on the trampoline effect to enable a family to bounce back rather than having to be too anxious about day-to-day survival to plan ahead?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Mr Chairman, the Government has pushed out an increasing number of schemes over the years to support Singaporeans in need.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: This is commendable, although I have concerns over the quantum of core aid schemes, as mentioned.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: To manage the many available schemes, the SupportGoWhere website was established where Singaporeans can search and get information in a single place.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: However, the application processes are still separately administered.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I wonder if the sheer number of named schemes can be housed under a smaller number of schemes, with officers empowered with the ability to cover more adjacent schemes so that there is less forwarding of applicants from one officer to another.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Awareness about various schemes has been identified as a problem previously, in a study conducted by Reaching Everyone for Active Citizenry (REACH) in 2014.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: It would be good to build upon a centralised platform to reduce the administrative strain of multiple means tests and application processes for all schemes.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Mr Chairman, applicants for financial assistance are burdened with presenting documents and also often face the embarrassment of having family members interviewed.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Would the Ministry consider having two formal means of application?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: For applicants who agree to presenting documents and having family members interviewed, they can do so.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: For those who have difficulty finding documents or do not wish to have their family members interviewed, they can instead choose to declare that the information that they provide is accurate.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Should they be found to have made a false declaration later, they could be subject to penalties.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Hence, I urge the Ministry to consider providing such a declarative option.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Also, SMTA offers assistance for three to six months, requiring applicants to re-apply frequently and providing them with less leeway or runway to plan ahead for their finances, while sometimes generating tremendous stress about the renewal, stress that can affect decision-making, impose bandwidth tax.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Can the Government consider a pilot test of a longer period of nine to 12 months for such assistance, to see if this generates better outcomes in terms of encouraging that mental energy and capacity to plan ahead, to turn their lives around and also lead to better outcomes for their children?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have been meeting various stakeholders to coordinate assistance for distressed families in my constituency.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I appreciate the usefulness of these collaborative sessions as it has been effective in providing holistic care.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We know who is doing what for whom in the family, thereby preventing duplication in efforts and plugging gaps.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: A feature which I have been hoping for is a centralised case file which all the stakeholders involved can access and link or refer to the relevant Government and other external assistance programmes.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This will be really helpful in speeding up delivery and reduce coordination costs.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would also like to ask about the befrienders with ComLink.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As the Ministry scales up this scheme, how is the recruitment of these volunteers progressing?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What are the main challenges encountered in attracting and retaining befrienders?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How is the Ministry reaching out to more Singaporeans to volunteer and participate in this worthy endeavour?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Chairman, I am heartened that KidSTART, which you started, will be expanded nationwide to support more eligible children in lower-income families.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The early indicators that children in the programme had better preschool attendance than their peers of similar socio-economic backgrounds were encouraging, so was the feedback from the parents and caregivers that they were better supported in their parenting journey.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: KidSTART organised an information session at a void deck in my constituency and the families just needed to come downstairs to attend the session.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, the parents were unable to attend and even if they attended, they were unable to concentrate unless someone helped to look after their children.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In addition, to enhance coordination for each case, we need to map out and identify which agencies to work with and share information within the team looking after the family.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Based on my experience, there is still room for improvement in information sharing and updating among the different agencies and volunteer groups.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: If the Ministry can provide more support and resources to facilitate consolidation and updating, that would be helpful as the assistance delivery process can be expedited.

speaker: The Chairman
text: For mentioning KidSTART, I give you more time.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As one of the main focus for this year's Budget Statement is to strengthen our social compact, it would be appropriate for me to echo my earlier calls on this.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The diverse choices of kindergartens give parents the option to select the centre which they deem to be in the child's best interest.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: They would obviously want their child to attend a preschool education centre which suits that child's learning style.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Apart from the child's learning style, there are parents who may also want their children to attend a preschool institution which provides religious knowledge.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The second suggestion I have, Sir, is for KiFAS to be made available for children who are Permanent Residents (PRs), provided that one of their parents or stepparents is a Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I have also suggested for MOE's Financial Assistance Scheme (FAS) to be extended to school-going children who have such parentage for the same reasons of elevating the financial burdens of such households where a Singapore Citizen has a child or stepchild who is a PR resulting from a transnational marriage.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We all know of the importance of early intervention services for children with developmental needs and in fostering inclusive preschool environments.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Families with children with developmental needs will face challenges in bringing up their children.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: They need greater support in identifying their children's needs early and in accessing the necessary tools and information.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Since 2019, the Ministry had introduced the Development Support Plus (DS-Plus) programme and Early Intervention Programme for Infants and Children (EIPIC) under two.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: In the same year, MSF had convened the Inclusive Preschool Workgroup (IPWG), which made several recommendations that have since been implemented.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: In general, what is the Ministry doing to better support families with children who have developmental needs?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: A 2006 research shows that infants and toddlers, particularly, benefit from these ratios.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Many early childhood educators believe that a ratio of one to three or four is higher and the best to allow for effective staff-child interaction.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: This also results in a smaller workload, lowers the stress level and improves the working conditions of the teachers.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Therefore, would MSF consider a review of staff-child ratios in childcare and infant care centres?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: I understand such ratios may be dependent on the number of teachers available.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: However, there has been anecdotal evidence that it may be due to the workload of these teachers.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: What are MSF's plans to tackle the turnover rate of preschool teachers?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am glad we are increasing the number of childcare places but we also need to consider the timing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At Yishun Glen, a new Build-To-Order (BTO) estate in Nee Soon East, most of the blocks have been completed and keys have been issued many months ago.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the childcare centre in the estate is still not completed.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: ECDA has not even announced the AOP who will run the centre.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Even if the centre is completed tomorrow, it will take months more for the operator to take over and renovate the centre.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Many of the estimated 179 children younger than seven living in Yishun Glen will need the childcare centre.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Surrounding childcare centres are also quite full, so, parents are stuck.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: In the future, can ECDA appoint the childcare centre operator much earlier and work with HDB to have the main contractor of the BTO project build and renovate the childcare centre for the operator?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: All these efforts will help save valuable time and resources and will mean that the childcare centre can be ready when residents move into their new homes.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Chairman, to nurture and develop children in the early years, families would need to consider all care options available to them.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: In 2013, ECDA was launched to integrate the regulation, planning, professional development and public education functions of MOE's preschool education branch and MSF's childcare division.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: ECDA now serves as the regulatory and developmental authority for the early childhood sector in Singapore, overseeing all aspects of children's development below the age of seven, across both kindergartens and childcare centres.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Since its inception, how effective has ECDA been in early childhood development?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Beyond ECDA, are there any initiatives MSF have introduced to assure parents that there will be accessible support in their children's early years?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Chairman, there is feedback from my residents that though there are vacancies in a particular infant care centre, the centre is unable to accept the children because of a shortage of infant care teachers.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For parents, it is also important for such centres to be near their homes to facilitate drop-offs and pick-ups.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Does the Ministry have plans to train more infant care specialists to meet the demand of our parents?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What are the challenges and obstacles in the recruitment and retention of these staff in this sector?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What more can be done to improve the working conditions of the teachers and reduce the attrition rate?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Mr Chairman, preschool education is an important formative experience for our young children.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: However, preschoolers from lower-income families do face more challenges in getting a good start in life.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: How will MSF assure parents in lower-income households that there will be accessible and affordable support in their children's early years?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Beyond increasing the accessibility and affordability of preschools, having an adequate and well-trained pool of educators is just as crucial.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Can MSF provide an update on the manpower situation in the preschool sector?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Sometimes, even having a proper meal break is a challenge.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: What is the preschool educator attrition rate in the past three years?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: How does MSF plan to reduce the attrition rate?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Are there any plans to increase the starting salaries of those working in non-AOPs?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I believe the disability community would like a detailed update from MSF on the progress of the masterplan.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: How will these two hub concepts be scaled in order to cover the many other adults who require the services?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Next, we should not wait for a COS to provide updates to the EMP2030.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: EMP2030 is unique in that it is for a duration of eight years versus the shorter five-year plans of the past.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: By 2030, most of the Ministry's public office holders, like the Minister and his team, would have moved on or be transferred.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: The assumptions underpinning these recommendations would have changed, in view of the rapid pace at which our society, our economy and our external environment have moved.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: I would expect that some of the recommendations may even be outdated.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Next, within just eight months of the release of EMP2030, the Government has already made several major announcements in the important aspects of mainstream Singapore: the Healthier SG movement to instil proactive and preventive healthcare is in place.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: MOE has announced its plan for future education to shift focus from the first 15 years to the next 50 years of one's life.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: The Ministry of National Development (MND) has announced new BTO ramp up plans and inclusive living for the elderly in the form of Community Service Apartments.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: How will MSF ensure the Enabling Masterplan includes and taps on these positive developments in the mainstream?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: How can we persuade the rest of the Government to adopt a universal design approach to service planning, so that the disabled will not be considered only as an afterthought?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I have a lot to thank my son for – for teaching me patience and resilience, for making me the person I am.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: He has also opened my eyes to a whole community of people with different abilities and the families who support them.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The more I learn about the diverse range of disabilities, the more I realise that there is a lot I do not know.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: One of the many things I am still learning is the appropriate terminology to use at times and I beg for indulgence.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are some specific needs within each disability group.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There is a different range of abilities and therefore differing potential amongst the persons with disabilities (PwDs).

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am heartened with the existing programmes in place to address the various needs of PwDs and their families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is encouraging to see the developments of the Enabling Masterplan over the years.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are, however, some areas which I would like to find out more about and have some views on.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: How are the efforts in addressing needs categorised and organised?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Is there some sort of framework to assess if we are adequately filling the gaps?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: My concern is while the broad efforts go some way to advance the interests of PwDs as a community, we may miss out specific issues that may only affect a particular group.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: For example, even within persons with intellectual disabilities (PwIDs), there are different levels of abilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: So, when we talk about lifelong learning and preparing them to live independently, could there be a finer resolution that could maximise the potential of each group?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Akin to the approach in our child and maternal health and well-being efforts, could we also look at streamlining some services that would make it easier for families to manage the care of PwDs?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I had spoken about Dr Chen Shiling in my previous speeches.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: She has now set up a clinic, IDHealth, that focuses on medical care of not just persons with intellectual disabilities but also their caregivers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Could we take a leaf from this approach and apply it to various other services?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I note that SG Enable is also already playing a role in being the one-stop spot for PwDs and their families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: How has this experience been and are there enhancements we can expect?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Lastly, I feel it is imperative to harness the resources and support from the community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I believe the Government can play a role to create the platform or structures to encourage ground-up effort.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: How do we sustain this and provide the necessary platforms for more people to come together?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I do hope to see more in our community step up to offer time or resources so that together, we can help to enhance support for PwDs and their families.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: It is not uncommon for us as Members of Parliament to come across residents seeking assistance on caregiving issues.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Just in the recent weeks, I met several residents from Bukit Batok East who had some challenges with caregiving.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In one case, a woman brought her sister, who has an intellectual disability.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Both her elderly parents had passed away, one after the other and rather unexpectedly.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The late mother was the main caregiver of the sister and my resident was at a loss as to how to now care for her sister.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In another case, a gentleman reached out to me for help after his elderly mother, who had been the primary caregiver of his brother with special needs, had to undergo heart surgery.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: He was the sole breadwinner and had to take time off work to care for his family members.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: During my house visits, I also meet many "aunties" who are caring for their elderly husbands.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: They do not have helpers and they lament about their challenges as they are not as strong as before.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Those who have children, do not want to burden their children.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: These are scenarios which are all too familiar to us.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Much has been said about the challenges of caregiving, especially when it relates to a long-term arrangement when the caregiver is the sole or primary caregiver, or where the person being cared for has some disabilities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are indeed many dimensions of the challenges including physical health and well-being of the caregiver and financial issues.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: These challenges are compounded further as the caregiver ages.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I am grateful for the various existing support that are in place.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: SG Enable and the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) have been very helpful in assisting with various issues that arise.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In the first two cases I mentioned above, I reached out to SG Enable and AIC and my residents are in the process of getting the assistance they need.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: But not all matters can be resolved simply and issues may not always be so straightforward.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Some arrangements proposed may not fully suit the preferences of the family.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I appreciate that there are limitations and it would not be reasonable or sustainable to expect agencies to provide the panacea to all problems.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: They need the respite so they can continue with their tasks and they need some assurance that they are not trapped in the circumstances alone, having to sacrifice their aspirations or well-being.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I quote, "We recognise that the burden on them is heavy.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I believe these are already being looked at.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: While the Government has a role in putting in place policies and support structures, I do hope to see families, extended families, stepping up to share the load of caring for their loved ones.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I understand that there is a partnership with CaringSG to work on Project 3i.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: I hope this platform is a genesis to the creation of more support options for caregivers, so that they can get the help, the respite and the assurance that they need to continue caring for their loved ones.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Chairman, part of the vocational training for PwDs in Singapore has focused on the hospitality, manufacturing and food and beverage (F&B) service sectors.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: As we continue to empower our PwDs, we must look into placing people in training or jobs, with a focus on their abilities and interests rather than their disabilities.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: Depending on their range of abilities, PwDs have the capacity to be employed across sectors and in different roles.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: As we see from examples in Australia, US and Japan, PwDs can be employed in a variety of sectors, ranging from retail to healthcare to graphic design and even transport technology.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: In Singapore, we have the UOB Scan Hub where over 30% of their staff are special needs employees, who digitise and archive documents.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: In India, department store Shoppers Stop has set up an organisation dedicated to help integrate PwDs into the fashion retail sector.

speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
text: In short, there are still many ways we can expand our training pathways for PwDs.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling, you can take your two cuts together.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I believe that lifelong learning opportunities and social inclusion activity must be availed to PwDs, just like all other Singaporeans.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: However, we know that such learning and social inclusion activities as well as respite care for caregivers should be provided in an integrated way to best help out PwDs and their families.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Can I ask for an update on the progress of EMP2030 implementation, especially in the provision of integrated learning, social inclusion and support services for PwDs and their caregivers?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: For earlier pilots like the Enabling Village at Lengkok Bahru, how is it achieving its goals and can such models be skilled to more regions?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: There is also an increase in nominal median gross monthly income for these Singaporeans between the same period.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: This is an encouraging progress, a step towards a more inclusive workforce and a demonstration that more PwDs can contribute to our economy.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Employment is not just essential for independence for adult PwDs, they provide dignity to them.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: This is especially important for adults who acquired disabilities due to unexpected events like accidents, or major health episodes like stroke, an increasing concern I have from the plight of the residents I see and help in my Meet-the-People sessions.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: To enable more PwDs to be employed, this will require the utmost support and actions from potential employers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This will hopefully provide more employment opportunities to PwDs near where they live.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: As part of our efforts to be an inclusive society, more should be done to help persons with disabilities who need customised work support and a structured environment to work in.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This is where the Enabling Business Hubs (EBHs) comes in.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Like hon Members Ms Denise Phua and Ms Ng Ling Ling, I too seek an update from the Ministry in relation to plans in this regard.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: These are respectable numbers and a testimony to the generosity of grant-makers, corporations and individuals in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The question arises as to what we should do to strengthen this culture of giving here.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I am uncertain as to whether this would move the needle by much.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I say this because over the past five years, the amounts of tax- deductible donations remained stable at about $1 billion.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: It seems to me that we need to do something more fundamental.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Successful organisations and people must be made to feel more invested in the lives of the less fortunate, so that they will feel morally obliged to do their part and donate.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I seek the hon Minister's views on this important topic that, in my view, will have an impact on how we keep together as one society.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: What is MSF doing to attract good people and leaders to this sector?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Supporting the marginalised and vulnerable families in Singapore is a whole-of-society responsibility.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Benny Chua, a franchisee of a ValuDollar store at Jalan Kukoh, joined in the mission to help bring dignity and hope to John, one of the residents at Transit Point@Jalan Kukoh, a shelter for displaced individuals run by New Hope.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chua shared: "They need opportunities to be able to uplift to support themselves and their families.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Hence, I am prepared to provide employment opportunities whenever I am hiring." It takes "heartwork" by many in the community to help one "John" at a time but in the end, our community will be that much more joyful and alive.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: If we go upstream and help youths get inspired, especially those who come from vulnerable families, we can change their destiny.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: The Singapore Business Federation (SBF) Foundation ran a pilot to connect 10 youths from Singapore Polytechnic with five "towkays" who joined the mission.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: One of the towkays, Jester Loi, a third-generation leader of Ya Kun, shared: "I get to see my company through the youths' lens and we all grew." Two of the students who participated shared: "Connections nowadays are very important. 'Youth Connections' gave me the opportunity to speak with business leaders.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: We gained friendships and grew our confidence." It takes "heartwork" by leaders to invest time with youths whom they do not ordinarily cross paths with, but that investment has potential to yield a hundred-fold.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: To uplift communities, we need another form of tripartism between corporates, social service agencies (SSAs) and their clients, and the Government.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Mr Chairman, SSAs form a vital part of our social support system, plugging system gaps and providing last-mile services to beneficiaries.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: When I was running Daughters Of Tomorrow as its Executive Director, it was a fledgling charity, and it benefited from financial management workshops held by Credit Suisse and social media marketing mentorship by Facebook employees.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: It helped the organisation greatly in enhancing its fundraising and outreach capabilities.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: But not many SSAs have a dedicated employee to lead such engagements with private companies.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Many would prefer to spend their operating budget on direct service personnel that executes services and programmes for beneficiaries.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Many SSAs dedicate their bandwidth to interventions and services, and do not have spare capacity to track and evaluate their programmes, which is crucial to show effectiveness and impact and to attract more funding to scale their solutions.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: When they do attempt to hire more staff, they find themselves unable to offer competitive salaries.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Some boards of charities are worried about optics or hindered by personal beliefs of board members around the notion of altruism or sometimes for whatever reasons, prefer a large reserve.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: These create constraints on management teams that try to be more progressive in adjusting their compensation system and results in talent risk for the social services, which then perpetuates the longstanding phenomenon of burnout amongst sector workers.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: And also, in addition to the Research Capability Development Service, MSF can replicate the Volunteer Manager Funding Scheme to help SSAs have a headcount in impact evaluation.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: The corporate partnerships are also an important function because it requires a different skillset and experience from community volunteer management, which requires some corporate background as well.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: This will have a catalysing effect to enable SSAs to excavate the potential of the private sector to contribute not just financial donations but also employees' skills and expertise for knowledge transfer.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: And this will help to shore the "heartware" that Ms Janet Ang spoke about.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: In summary, there is still room to optimise our sector funding for capability enhancements for SSAs.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: First, on human resources (HR), besides funding competitive salaries of supported staff, can MSF please facilitate higher provisions for hiring of foreign staff in services such as day activity centres for the elderly and the disabled and special schools.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: This is so critical as competition for manpower becomes more intense.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Second, subsidise the costs of corporate services and compliance, such as Executive Directors, Finance, HR, Information Technology (IT) and Audit for charities providing essential services for the sector.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: As larger and needed charities get called to do more, they are also being held to higher and higher standards of reporting and accountability; adding to the cost of compliance and management.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: And lastly, seek regular feedback on Government donation matching schemes meant to encourage fundraising.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
text: Do not make it harder for charities than it already is.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Chairman, I am glad that as a nation, we have started the conversation on how we should value all work equally, whether these are "head", "heart" or "hands" work.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Today, I would like to advocate for "heart" work, that is, jobs and careers in the community care and services sector.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: We, as a nation, had pledged not to leave anyone behind; and a competent and effective social service sector is crucial to fulfil this vision.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: How can the Government attract good people to join our SSAs?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: How will MSF retain them, support, and empower them to excel?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: These are important questions which we must get right to build a united nation with strong bonds, based on equality and social mobility.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Our SSAs are responsible for the delivery of assistance to the vulnerable amongst us.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: When they do their jobs well, they uplift not only the lives of this segment but our whole society.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: How will the Ministry affirm the efforts and contributions of our SSAs and support them to thrive?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Their backgrounds in social services should be treated as equally as those from other sectors.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: In other words, our social compact hinges on the tripartite understanding between individuals and families, the Government and the community.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: A social compact that is deemed fair by all segments of society, will strengthen social capital and foster trust.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: And this is what will enable us to progress together as a nation.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: External developments, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, US-China tensions and the ongoing Russia-Ukraine war have altered, the geopolitical milieu we live in.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Domestically, we must manage the impact of trends, such as the ageing population and slowing social mobility.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Cumulatively, these trends can put a strain on our social compact.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Hence, it is imperative that we support our social service partners to strengthen our social compact, amidst internal and external uncertainties.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: As such, how will MSF recognise the efforts of our social service partners and better support them to strive.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Chairman, the saying "it takes a village to raise a child" helps us appreciate how much more it takes to care for the underprivileged, vulnerable and those in need in our society.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: An ecosystem of willing and capable social service partners, each playing a role and contributing its strength and resources is key in keeping our social safety net and support system strong for those among us in need, to leave no one behind as far as possible.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Social service partners not only include our hundreds of SSAs who provide the needed direct services across Singapore, but also companies who provide donations, staff, volunteers, employment opportunities as well as academia who conduct social intervention research, social entrepreneurs and many silent contributors who quietly nurture, enable and build lives around us as they see the needs.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: In recent years, this has been the students in computing and data sciences.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Their work is meaningful as they provide social care and interventions to those in need.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We face long-term trends such as a declining birth rate and an ageing population.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: These will lead to a rise in the need for social care and services.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: How will MSF better support our social service professionals and better support the social service sector to have adequate manpower and good working conditions?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We must focus our minds in ensuring that this large group of professionals are paid competitively, so as to retain the best talents in this important sector.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The vision to strengthen families and sustain social mobility is a common one we all share.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Singapore has invested in the education and well-being of its people.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Singaporeans enjoy stable employment, own homes, have the means to start families and lead meaningful lives.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is a hope that we want to keep alive as a society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At MSF, we also want all families to enjoy such resilience and confidence in their future.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In short, we want all families to achieve the "3Ss": stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Stability, where families are strong and have the means to weather the ups and downs in life.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When families face challenges, they weather them because of mutual support from their children, siblings, parents and the extended family.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Those who face severe challenges can also look to support from the Government.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Self-reliance, where families have a strong sense of ownership.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our society is strong because many Singaporeans continue to have this belief.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MSF and our partners see many families who receive help and are motivated not only to do better for themselves and their children, but to actually give back and uplift others.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Social mobility, where families will always have opportunities to progress and better their circumstances, and where they can aspire for their children to have a better and brighter future.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Sustaining social mobility across generations is the most important assurance we can offer to families in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The "3Ss" – stability, self-reliance and social mobility – is MSF's hope for all families, but especially for lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is Singapore's unique approach to addressing inequality – we keep social mobility alive by enabling self-reliance and building stability.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have seen elsewhere how rising social inequality leads to the stratification of society, growing distrust for the Government and increasing disunity amongst the people.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To remain a united people, Singapore must do all we can to avoid walking this same path.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have proven to ourselves, during the COVID-19 pandemic that we are a people who will help one another through difficult times.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As we look ahead, we must build our social capital and strengthen our social compact as Mr Seah Kian Peng and Ms Ng Ling Ling have also suggested.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But as they also suggested, this means it is not just what the Government can do.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is also what individuals, families and the community can do together, so that together, we strengthen families and sustain social mobility.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The "how" is as important as the "what".

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Chairman, families are the bedrock of our society, where values are transmitted and our characters are shaped.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A supportive family nurtures children to become compassionate members of society, able to pursue their aspirations, achieve social mobility for their family and give back to society.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A strong nation is built on strong families.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Government has invested greatly in families to support them across all stages.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Members may also access these materials through the MP@SGPARL app.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Together with these latest measures, families are supported across all stages in life.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For those starting a family, we will provide them with greater support in securing their first home.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Newlyweds are supported in laying strong foundations to their marriage, such as through marriage preparation programmes and mentoring support from their Licensed Solemnisers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When couples go on to have children, they are supported in the cost of raising their children through the increase in the Baby Bonus Cash Gift and Child Development Account (CDA).

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Parents with children of preschool ages have access to affordable and quality preschools, with more places to be created.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Families caring for PwDs have enhanced support for lifelong learning, employment opportunities, as well as caregiving support.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We also support our seniors in ageing well.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Seniors are supported through preventive health, active ageing programmes and care services.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are building towards a society that empowers seniors to live healthier lives, be socially engaged and contribute meaningfully.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The top-up to the ComCare Endowment Fund provides more resourcing and certainty for MSF in supporting lower-income families through ComCare, amid high inflation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: ComLink has also been rolled out to proactively support families with children in rental homes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our efforts continue, as we strive to make Singapore a place where families thrive.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Last year, during the Year of Celebrating SG Families, MSF launched the Singapore Made for Families 2025 Plan, a three-year plan that outlines how the Government, community partners, businesses and individuals can, together, create a Singapore where all families are valued and supported.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As families navigate various milestones, our goal is to ensure they are equipped with the necessary family and parenting skills.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked about the efforts of FFL, to strengthen families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: FFL started with broad-based public education campaigns and resources.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There will be families that need more targeted support.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Today, there are FSCs which provide integrated and multidisciplinary services to meet the diverse needs of families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The services they offer include marriage preparation programmes, parenting programmes, family counselling and divorce support programmes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have seen positive outcomes from these efforts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, participants of our marriage preparation programme, Prevention and Relationship Education Programme (PREP), report better communication skills with their spouse.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We know that all couples aspire to have a strong relationship and a strong family.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: FFL and FAM@FSC are there on the ground, to provide support to them if they need it.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Dr Shahira Abdullah spoke about support for single unwed mothers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our policies reflect the value our society places on parenthood within marriage.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, we also empathise with the challenges faced by single unwed parents.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There is appropriate welfare support for them too.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In providing support, we put weight on their child's well-being and supporting them in their caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: HDB also assesses their requests for housing holistically, based on their individual circumstances.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The family plays an important role in caring for its loved ones even in old age.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Increasingly, the LPA and ACP will be important ways that families have the assurance that they are respecting the wishes and intent of their loved ones, who may no longer be able to express their wishes when they lose their mental capacity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In response to Mr Henry Kwek, we are making progress in encouraging adoption of LPAs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Some Members have raised the issue of possible abuse of LPAs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, others have asked for the process to be simpler and cheaper.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Public Guardian will continue to be mindful of these considerations and I seek the support of Members to understand that the Public Guardian has to balance convenience and cost, with appropriate safeguards.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: What I have covered are broad-based efforts to strengthen families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will also extend additional support to lower-income families, through targeted programmes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These families often face complex and interlocking challenges, which cannot be addressed by one agency or partner.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These issues need to be addressed proactively, early, and in a coordinated way, preventing them from becoming entrenched.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One example is KidSTART, which is targeted at children in lower-income families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Through KidSTART, parents are empowered to be confident and competent caregivers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Efforts begin at the hospital, with families given close support through home visits as the child grows older.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is a major effort to move upstream in our support for children from lower-income families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Minister of State Sun Xueling will share more on this.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: ComLink further ensures that children from lower-income families are provided with a good start in life and supported on a journey of progress.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Introduced in 2019, it supports families with children living in rental housing by connecting them to community resources and Government services.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Like the localised FFL presence that I spoke about just now in each town, ComLink depends on a contingent of volunteers working closely with officers at the SSOs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Over 2,400 volunteers have been recruited to support various ComLink efforts such as outreach, befriending and programmes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One such volunteer is Shen Jun, who has helped Mr Wong, aged 68, improve the circumstances of his family.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Wong was worried he would not be able to find employment, given his age.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But with Shen Jun's support, Mr Wong secured a full-time job as a security officer.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: His family is now no longer on ComCare assistance.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Shen Jun regularly visits them and shares relevant resources and information, such as HDB launch dates, knowing that Mr Wong aspires to own a flat.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: He also shares information on bursary awards for their son, who is in primary school, to help them with their expenses.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Wong and his family are grateful to Shen Jun for his support.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For families that demonstrate a strong commitment to do their part to create better conditions for their children, we want to be able to support them better – this is our approach in our new social compact.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We intend to tailor sustained support to encourage them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our aim is for them to achieve the "3Ss" quicker.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are working out the specifics and intend to share details later this year.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Apart from lower-income families, families caring for children with developmental needs also need additional attention.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Minister of State Sun Xueling will elaborate on our plans to increase early intervention capacity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will also provide support for families caring for PwDs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Efforts are underway to progressively implement the 29 recommendations of the Masterplan.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This follows the recommendation to provide support services to enable PwDs to live independently and well in, and with, the community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Hub will reach out to PwDs and their caregivers in its region to understand their needs, link them to relevant support and provide onsite services such as continuous learning programmes and respite care for caregivers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua will elaborate on support for PwDs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Integral to our efforts to strengthen families and uplift those in need are our partners.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Joan Pereira, Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman, Ms Ng Ling Ling and Ms Janet Ang have asked how we will recognise and continue to support these efforts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In recognition of our SSAs' invaluable efforts, 2023 has been dedicated as the Year of Celebrating Social Service Partners.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Significant contributions by SSAs are also recognised through the annual MSF Volunteer and Partner Awards and Community Chest Awards.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
