text: Behind the successful delivery of social services by the SSAs are those who provide resources, funds and manpower – the Government, philanthropists and donors, as well as volunteers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Over the years, we have witnessed donors stepping forward and have developed and strengthened mechanisms to support the social service sector in meeting emerging needs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Tote Board Social Service Fund, for instance, supports more than 70 programmes serving over 362,000 clients, in partnership with various Government agencies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As social needs further evolve, access to generous financial support remains a key enabler of the sector.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Beyond financial support, a strong core of passionate and competent professionals is equally crucial.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As raised by Mr Seah Kian Peng and Ms Denise Phua, they need to be given due recognition and supported in their work.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, measures must be taken to better attract, train and retain staff.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To support SSAs in this area, we have completed the review of the National Council of Social Service (NCSS) Sector Salary Guidelines, to keep pace with wage realities in the market and account for changes in job responsibilities, as well as salaries of comparable roles in competing markets.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I strongly encourage SSAs to adopt the guidelines to continue to attract and retain talent, and MSF and NCSS will support their efforts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Funding for MSF and NCSS-funded programmes will also be adjusted accordingly.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Also working tirelessly alongside our sector professionals, are our volunteers.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NCSS will be rolling out new schemes under the Community Capability Trust to help SSAs build capabilities for better volunteer management.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Ms Carrie Tan has also asked about support for our SSAs in building capabilities in research and evaluation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We agree that this is important and there are existing support and initiatives in place.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SSAs may also tap on research advisory support through NCSS' network of volunteer research consultants, and subsidised research courses and workshops offered by the Social Service Institute and universities.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Chairman, beyond SSAs, there are many more who make a difference in the social sector – including businesses and the Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs).

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Businesses are a key touchpoint for different segments of society.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At its very core, businesses provide employment – the first step to achieving stability, self-reliance and social mobility, the "3Ss".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Businesses also help shape Singapore into a family-friendly and inclusive society through FWAs for caregivers and inclusive hiring practices for PwDs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Furthermore, businesses possess a wealth of resources and many have sought to share this, weaving giving into their DNA.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Murali Pillai and Ms Janet Ang said that more could be done to build the culture of giving.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are heartened by and appreciate SBF Foundation's initiatives on this front, and in particular, as part of the Youth Connections Pilot, as Ms Janet Ang has shared.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This demonstrates the strong impact that businesses can make beyond economic returns.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Moving forward, we will continue to partner businesses to promote and encourage sustainable philanthropy, which looks to businesses and Singaporeans making sustained contributions, beyond episodic giving of money and goods.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I am glad that banks such as DBS, Maybank and UOB have joined us on this initiative and that retail brands like Eu Yan Sang are matching their customers' donations.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the coming years, we believe more businesses will come on board Change for Charity.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our hope is that more businesses and organisations will not just stop with Change for Charity but come up with creative ways to leverage their expertise.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In each business and organisation is a wellspring of good that can be achieved, tapping on the business's assets, their expertise and time of its people.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For instance, in 2022, Mendix, a software company, gathered over 400 developers for an international hackathon on issues faced by non-profit organisations, including our SSAs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, New Hope Community Services now has an app that allows social workers to view their programme activities easily, facilitating service delivery.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Another example is the Community Uplift Programme by UOL and the Pan Pacific Hotels Group.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Through this, UOL and Pan Pacific tap on their resources to provide enriching experiences like rock climbing and art classes for children from ComLink families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This offers the children opportunities to bond with their families and participate in activities not easily accessible to them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But more importantly, by bringing these children and their families out of their everyday settings into venues such as hotels managed by their group, the children are exposed to a greater breadth of career choices.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This broadens their outlook and inspires them to dream bigger and climb higher in life.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As for the IHLs, they are where our social sector professionals acquire the knowledge and skills to work effectively.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Researchers and academics also contribute invaluable insights to inform our policies and practice.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, the research project on Identifying Positive Adaptive Pathways in Low-Income Families in Singapore conducted by the National University of Singapore (NUS) researchers informs efforts to better support families in working towards the "3Ss", particularly in times of economic hardship.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our work through ComLink family coaches and befrienders provides precisely these opportunities to build such resilience, towards the "3Ss".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I hope the research will be as informative to the refinement of ComLink as Growing Up in Singapore Towards Healthy Outcomes (GUSTO) has been for KidSTART.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The study also demonstrated that a mothers' physical and mental well-being during pregnancy had a large impact on their child's development.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This led us to focusing on reaching more mothers at the antenatal stage so that they can benefit earlier from KidSTART.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To harness this spirit for a stronger collective impact, we look forward to greater collaborations with universities and academics to develop research.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MSF has begun this work through the Asian Family Conference, bringing together researchers, policymakers and practitioners across the region to exchange learning points and leveraging this research to inform policies and practice.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The intention is to build up a robust knowledge base of family-centric research that can inform social policy and practice in Singapore and beyond – something Ms Ng Ling Ling asked for.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: SSAs can both contribute to and tap on this base of knowledge as resources for their work.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In particular, there is a need for local research that speaks to our context, taking on a family-centric approach, our unique socio-cultural environment and the cultural nuances of the diverse communities in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Chairman, allow me to continue in Malay, please.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: (In Malay):   Chairman, families are at the centre of what we do and will remain the focus of the Government’s efforts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will strengthen support in the community as they go through the various stages in their family journey, from the point a couple contemplates marriage, to when they start a family, to raising their children and so on.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Government is committed to building a better future for all, and we will leave no one behind.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have introduced several initiatives to better support Malay/Muslim families.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: At the same time, we must encourage our young to dream big and to work towards those dreams.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: One of the ways is to provide role models and positive influences.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The Government will work closely with our partners to provide stronger support for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: (In English): Chairman, strengthening families and sustaining social mobility for our people is a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Our SSAs, social enterprises, businesses, community groups, academia and more have been invaluable partners.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In this Year of Celebrating Social Service Partners, I encourage Singaporeans to join us in applauding the contributions of our partners and encourage more partners to join hands with us.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Chairman, I thank Members for their views on preschool education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Just as families are the bedrock of our society, children are the future of families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I will share on MSF's approach to give every child a good start in life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our efforts are part of the whole-of-society plan, A Singapore Made for Families 2025, which was launched by Deputy Prime Minister Heng last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If we want a society made for families to thrive, each and every one of us has a role – the Government, the community, such as SSAs or businesses, and families, including parents, children, siblings and other caregivers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is our social compact – to weave together a larger circle of care to support families to achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: A good start in life begins at birth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government is committed to supporting couples as they embark on their parenting journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While families may have different caregiving needs and preferences, parental care and support remain crucial in anchoring and shaping our children's development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Findings from the GUSTO study, which Minister Masagos mentioned earlier, suggest that mothers' responsiveness to their child's signals or needs in infancy, also called maternal sensitivity, was linked to brain development in early childhood.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Today, most infants are cared for in a home-based setting by caregivers such as parents and family members while around one in five infants are in centre-based infant care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the playgroup years, there is also a growing segment of families who are enrolling their children in preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng and Mr Fahmi Aliman have asked how we will assure parents that they will be supported in their children's earliest years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have also been ramping up the infant care workforce, something Ms Joan Pereira raised.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are tapping on a wider pool of local and foreign allied infant educators and programme helpers who can jointly contribute up to 50% of the staff in infant care bays.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Dr Shahira Abdullah asked about lowering staff-child ratios in infant care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our staff-child ratio requirements are minimum requirements to ensure the safety and well-being of children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These are calibrated based on the needs of children at different ages.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In practice, many preschool operators operate with more staff to the same number of children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, any changes to the minimum staff-child ratio can impact overall manpower demand and availability of services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our staff-child ratio requirements are, hence, designed to work with other regulations to ultimately provide a safe and conducive environment for our children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Seah asked about the progress of the EYDF review.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Seah and Mr Fahmi also mentioned that centre-based care may not be the preferred solution for all families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are mindful that many parents want more options in caring for their young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Under the ForwardSG exercise, we are studying how we can better support families, given what we know about the importance of the involvement of parents in the early years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Regardless of one's choice of caregiving arrangements, it is important for families to be well equipped to navigate the joys and challenges of raising young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Minister Masagos spoke about our plans to expand Families for Life @ Community, or FFLC in short, islandwide to enable families to access parenting and grandparenting programmes more easily.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In this expansion, we will work closely with SSAs, schools, volunteers, community and corporate partners as well as health clusters to equip families with the skills to nurture and care for young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are also exploring different parenting programmes and will promote parenting programmes which are science-based and outcome-driven.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For children aged three and above, preschool can be the best option to meet parents' caregiving needs while supporting children's development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: In this way, preschools provide an important service to help working parents balance between their work and caregiving responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our preschools complement the important role that parents play, giving parents the assurance that their children are well taken care of while providing a nurturing and supportive environment where children can grow and develop holistically.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: International research shows us that attending quality preschool can boost our children's confidence and social skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Additionally, our local data shows that children who attended preschool from three years onwards are less likely to require additional learning support in primary school.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To meet the growing demand for preschools, we have worked with preschool operators to more than double the number of preschool places over the past decade.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the timing of building new childcare centres.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA works closely with agencies, such as HDB and the Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA), to develop new preschools together with new housing developments so that they are conveniently located near families with young children and can be operational shortly after residents move in.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ECDA will continue to work with agencies on the timing of preschool openings to facilitate faster enrolment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked how we will ensure there are enough preschool educators to support the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To encourage more educators to join the sector, the Government has been enhancing educators' career progression and professional development, as well as undergoing a review of the working conditions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To keep salaries competitive, we announced salary enhancements for educators in Government-supported preschools last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to work with preschools to reach out to different sources of local and foreign manpower, who have the right aptitude and passion for working with children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These could include mid-career individuals, back-to-work women and stay-at-home mothers among others.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked about the affordability of preschools which are not Government-funded.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We expect median fees to decrease even further, as we had lowered fee caps at Government-supported preschools at the start of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Families' out-of-pocket expenses are lower than fee caps after factoring in subsidies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More families can enjoy fee caps at Government-supported preschools as we expand capacity to allow 80% of preschoolers to have a place in a Government-supported preschool by around 2025, up from over 60% today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked about extending the KiFAS to children from lower-income households enrolled in non-AOP or non-MOE Kindergartens.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our priority is to ensure that Singaporean children have access to affordable and quality preschool services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As such, KiFAS is extended only to Singapore Citizen children attending AOP and MOE Kindergartens, which are publicly accessible to all families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There are sufficient places in these kindergartens nationally to serve lower-income families who want to enrol their child into a kindergarten programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will continue to invest heavily in improving access to affordable and quality preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This spending is expected to go up significantly over the next few years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: While we continue to invest in our preschools to support all families, we also recognise that lower-income families and those who have children with developmental needs may face additional challenges.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Fahmi Aliman have asked how MSF can provide greater support for lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will do so through providing more upstream and targeted support, journeying with lower-income families through various life milestones to empower them to uplift themselves and their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This support will begin from the early years, which are critical for children's development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The GUSTO study I mentioned earlier found links between mothers' well-being during pregnancy and their children's later development, and this is why the KidSTART programme supports families as early as possible, starting even before the child is born.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng will be glad to know that we have supported over 6,200 children since KidSTART was started in 2016.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have closely studied the impact of the programme on families and seen positive outcomes for parents and children alike.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Through regular home visits, KidSTART equips parents with the skills and knowledge to support their children's development, health and nutrition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Parents in KidSTART families who received these visits showed improvements in their parenting skills, such as confidence and ability to interact well with their children and reduced parenting stress.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Their children also improved in their socio-emotional and daily living skills which is demonstrated in their ability to cooperate with others, manage their emotions and self-control.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These are significant outcomes in early childhood interventions and have far-reaching consequences, including influencing many outcomes later in life, such as educational attainment and employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister Wong mentioned in his Budget speech, we will expand KidSTART nationwide to offer the programme to all eligible families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We expect to support about 80% of children from eligible lower-income families, up from around 20% today, beginning with children born this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These eligible mothers-to-be will be supported by a multidisciplinary team during their pregnancy, to help them keep well physically and mentally before childbirth.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: After their child is born, the new mothers will continue to be supported by KidSTART practitioners in the home, community and preschool settings, to empower them to continue to nurture their children's growth and development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: KidSTART is an open programme and eligible mothers are welcomed to join at any point during their pregnancy or after their child is born.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: KidSTART's success is possible only through partnering our community and corporates, which have given holistic support to families across the social, health and education domains.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are keen to work with more partners as we reach out to more families in the next phase of KidSTART's expansion.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also continue to enhance coordination with our partners to better support KidSTART families, as Ms Joan Pereira had suggested.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our data shows that about 80% of children aged three to four from lower-income families are enrolled into preschool.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is lower than the enrolment rate for their peers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Lower-income families are faced with complex challenges, including searching for stable employment, housing, or perhaps, managing medical issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Hence, early preschool enrolment for their young children may not be a priority.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have made some progress through KidSTART and the Preschool Outreach Programme in reaching out to lower-income families to help facilitate their children's preschool enrolment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have also taken decisive steps to enhance preschool affordability for lower-income families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Currently, they can pay as low as $3 per month for full-day childcare at AOP preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, more needs to be done to close the preschool enrolment gap between children from lower-income families and their peers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We hope that with a facilitated enrolment process, parents from lower-income families will work with us and help to enrol their children into preschool by age three.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Beyond preschool enrolment, we also recognise that children from lower-income families may need more support to attend preschool regularly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: KidSTART practitioners will work closely with preschools to address barriers to regular preschool attendance for KidSTART children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: ComLink, which Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua will elaborate on later, also addresses attendance barriers and other family needs holistically.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Under the ForwardSG exercise, we are studying how to further support children from lower-income families in preschools, including considering different ways to encourage timely enrolment and regular attendance.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Together, these moves will lay a stronger foundation to help children from lower-income families progress in life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: By intervening early to support subsequent education and life outcomes, we hope to sustain social mobility across generations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Seah Kian Peng spoke about families who have children with developmental needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We agree with him that we need to support these families to identify their children's needs early and ensure that they receive the necessary support in a timely manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: As Minister Masagos shared, children with developmental needs may face considerable wait times for enrolment at an early intervention (EI) centre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have focused our efforts on increasing the number of places in Government-funded EI programmes so that these children can receive support earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will launch more EI centres over the next two years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The two EI centres which I announced last year will begin operations in Fernvale Woods and Bukit Batok by the end of this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will also triple the number of EI places offered under the PPIP programme by March 2024.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: To ensure that the PPIP programme is an affordable option for families, we will lower out-of-pocket expenses for the programme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: From 1 July this year, ECDA will introduce caps on the maximum amount that families pay for PPIP.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have also implemented initiatives to enhance inclusion and support for children with developmental needs in preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Inclusive Support Programme was piloted in October 2021 to integrate the provision of EI services within preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Families of children enrolled in the pilot had found the pilot helpful, as children can now benefit from preschool and EI services in one location rather than shuttling between different locations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Families need to be adequately supported to make informed decisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Parents have given feedback that they have found the guide to be useful.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have since made vernacular versions to make it accessible to more parents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: With everyone's support, we can forge a more caring and inclusive society, beginning in the early years, where families provide the first line of support and care for their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: More children receive timely support in early intervention centres and preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: And the community embraces the diversity of abilities in children, supporting all children to play, learn, contribute and participate meaningfully alongside one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In Mandarin):   It is important that we continue to build strong and resilient families, which are the bedrock of society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Families play an indispensable role in caring and raising our children, especially in their earliest years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Families encourage our children to progress towards their aspirations, help them develop the right mindset to overcome challenges and inspire them to take the best of the opportunities presented to them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: These are the most valuable lessons that will carry our children through life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We recognise that parents may have different needs and preferences when caring for their children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: At the playgroup years, between one to three years old, there is also a growing segment of families who are enrolling their children in preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government is studying how to better support families with infants, to meet varying preferences and needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: For children aged three years and above, preschool can be the best option to meet parents' caregiving needs while supporting children's development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have made good progress in improving access to affordable and quality preschools and will continue to invest heavily in our preschools.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: There are also some families that need more help in their journey.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We will step up our efforts to provide targeted and timely support for children from lower-income families, as well as families who have children with developmental needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We need community partners and volunteers to come alongside such families to create a strong tapestry of support, empowering them and their children to rise above their circumstances.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Preschools and early childhood educators also play an important role, working closely with parents and the community to equip these children with the tools that they need to develop and thrive alongside their peers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: It takes a whole-of-society effort to build a Singapore Made for Families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Let us work closely together to empower parents to give our children the opportunity to achieve their fullest potential – by nurturing their early growth and development at home, and enrolling them in preschool by age three, so that they can benefit from quality preschool education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: (In English): Chairman, parents should have the assurance that their children will be well-supported and have good access to opportunities to progress in life, regardless their starting points.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This is a commitment that we want to make and a journey on which we want to walk with our families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are all familiar with the phrase "it takes a village to raise a child".

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: What it means for us today is that it takes many helping hands to give every child a good start in life and build a Singapore Made for Families together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Our preschools, SSAs, healthcare institutions, and other community partners have made good progress in supporting families with young children.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Government will continue to work with them in a more coordinated manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Even as we work together to strengthen support for families, every family must be willing to come forward, seize the opportunities presented to them, and do their part to achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The challenges each family faces too, are unique.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, I will focus my speech on: one, families with loved ones who are PwDs; and two, lower-income families with children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our vision for Singapore is to be a caring and inclusive society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: One with a big heart, and one where PwDs are empowered to pursue their aspirations, realise their potential and participate in civic life, just as anyone would.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked about the success and challenges of our Enabling Masterplans over the years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since our first Masterplan in 2007, we have made good progress in areas spanning education, sport, assistive technology, our built environment, public transport and societal norms.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These improvements have empowered PwDs to live life to the fullest.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I first met Aloysius and his father Kagan, when we travelled to Bahrain for the Asian Youth Para Games (AYPG) two years ago.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He has cerebral palsy and is paralysed in all four limbs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: He attends school at the Cerebral Palsy Alliance Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Aloysius communicates with the help of an assistive technology device, uses a wheelchair and is able get around on public transport as our bus and train network is largely barrier-free.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For me, cheering on Aloysius at the AYPG felt no different from cheering for our able-bodied athletes at other major games.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I witnessed first-hand Aloysius' steely determination to overcome his stronger and more experienced opponents, never mind that it was his international debut in 2021.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And overcame them he did, making history as he brought home a coveted Gold medal.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, Aloysius is setting his sights on attaining a sports scholarship and representing Singapore at the Paralympics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I see a fellow human being, wanting nothing more than just to become the best version of himself, just like any of us, disability or otherwise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our hope that with the right support, PwDs too can realise their potential and live life to the fullest.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since our first Enabling Masterplan, we have come a long way.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Ms Rahayu noted, a key challenge in building an inclusive society lies in meeting varied needs across a diverse range of disabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our approach must be one of working with PwDs, caregivers, disability sector professionals and community partners, as we periodically review our policies and programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This partnership approach ensures that specific needs are understood and allows stakeholders to work on solutions together.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Because of my work in the disability space, I was privileged to have been part of some very meaningful and some very powerful conversations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Meaningful because many points raised came from a position of care and love.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Powerful because a lot of what has been said were real and vulnerable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Months on, I still "hear" these questions in my heart: "After graduation, will my autistic daughter be able to find a job that she can excel in?" "Can my brother and I enjoy a basketball game at the neighbourhood court, just like the rest?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But because he plays from a wheelchair, we sometimes get weird stares." "How much longer can I last?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I feel like I am going to burn out very soon." "Ah Boy has intellectual disability!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Who will take care of him after I leave this world?" Hearing all this has only powered me and my colleagues' resolve to do our best for disability-inclusion in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: EMP2030 is no panacea, but it sets out a broad vision for the next eight years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, a masterplan is of little use if it is merely the exercise of putting pen to paper.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To bring the plan to life, we need everyone's buy-in, support and more importantly, action.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Denise Phua is right that we must tap on mainstream initiatives to support PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Where mainstream support is not adequate to meet the needs of PwDs, we provide additional targeted support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For students with more severe needs, special education (SPED) schools provide more intensive and customised support to help them thrive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Opportunities are also created for students from both SPED and mainstream schools to learn together and interact meaningfully.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Denise Phua also asked about the implementation progress of the EMP2030 recommendations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Inclusive communities play an essential role in enabling PwDs to live well and to participate actively in the community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling also asked about plans to scale existing initiatives and provide integrated support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: When MSF and SG Enable opened the Enabling Village in 2015, it was the first inclusive community space in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It demonstrated how we can create communities where PwDs participate as integral and contributing members.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Building on our experience with the Enabling Village or EV, as it is affectionately known to some of us, we plan to bring services closer to where PwDs live and we are doing this via two new pilots.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: A satellite site will also be set up in Heartbeat @ Bedok.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The ESH will have an outreach team, which will actively engage PwDs and their families living in Tampines and Bedok, especially those who are not currently enrolled in any disability services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In addition, community befrienders will be matched to those who need more support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At the ESH, PwDs can take part in social activities to interact with neighbours and volunteers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They can also attend courses to pick up new skills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Caregivers who need a short break can also make use of drop-in respite care services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The ESH will also work with local partners to encourage inclusion within our neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For instance, residents with and without disabilities can join in community activities together, or even volunteer as befrienders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Companies in the area can offer employment opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With your active participation, we can foster more inclusive communities rooted in these ESHs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The second pilot is the EBHs, which will bring jobs closer to where PwDs live.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Many PwDs can and want to be gainfully employed with dignity, not just for charity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This view was also echoed by Ms Ng.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Beyond the benefit to the individual PwDs, companies with inclusive hiring practices find stronger empathy amongst co-workers and a more cohesive workforce.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Some employers might be keen to hire inclusively but may not know how to go about it.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Collaborating with employers and industry associations, the EBH will showcase inclusive hiring practices and help companies implement these practices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For instance, by re-designing jobs so that tasks can be done by PwDs and using technology to enhance productivity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Ms Ng highlighted, job coaches play an important role in helping employers looking to hire PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: There are currently about 300 job coaches providing a range of disability employment support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The EBH will also have a team of job coaches on site.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The EMP2030 Employment Taskforce will explore building up job coach capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The EBH will also help to identify other suitable employers in the region and match them with PwDs who have the necessary skills and if necessary, prepare them for those jobs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Murali Pillai would be happy to know that the first EBH will be opening its doors later this year in Jurong West.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Miss Rachel Ong asked about alternative training pathways for PwDs to work in more sectors.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, PwDs can access vocational training through SPED schools, the School-to-Work Transition Programme and SG Enable's Enabling Academy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These programmes prepare them for work in a range of sectors, including horticulture, online retail and facility services.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are continually looking for employers and industries who are keen to hire inclusively so that PwDs can be employed in meaningful roles.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For a start, the first hub in Jurong West will focus on showcasing how PwDs can be a part of the logistics industry.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Beyond EBH, we are also expanding the capacity of sheltered workshops.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This will help to alleviate the waitlists for sheltered workshops, which are currently operating at almost full capacity.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: MSF will continue to monitor the demand for adult disability services and will also review service models as needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Beyond PwDs, we must also look out for their caregivers and family members.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We work closely with our partners to ensure that caregivers are also supported.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam asked for an update on the AfA for Caregivers of PwDs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The AfA is supporting Project 3i, a caregiver-led initiative to provide a network of social and emotional support for caregivers and to equip them with caregiving skills.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is being piloted at two locations: Boon Lay and Kampong Glam.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Everyone plays a part in making disability-inclusion a reality.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: How we perceive PwDs and how we behave around them are markers of how inclusive we are as a society.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Chair, allow me some time to share about Ms Sophie Soon.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I got to know Sophie in 2021, when she flew our flag high at the Tokyo Paralympics.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Whenever one meets Sophie, one can almost be sure that Orinda, her Golden-Labrador Retriever buddy, will be by her side.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Orinda's love for Sophie, though, transcends the usual pet-and-owner proportions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Sophie is visually impaired and Orinda is Sophie's guide dog.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Guide dogs are specially bred, and they go through stringent assessment and training for 18 months before they are matched to their potential human pals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Unfortunately, a lack of awareness surrounding guide dogs meant the duo sometimes find themselves in awkward situations, to say the least.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In January this year, Sophie and Orinda were all stoked about attending their first Candlelight concert until they were stopped by security and Sophie got asked some questions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: She was asked, "You want to watch the show, right?" by security, "How you see?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: You cannot see, right?" This was in January this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Last November, Sophie and Orinda were again the subject of scrutiny, when a fellow train passenger's unfounded fear that Orinda poses a safety risk made its way into the media.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Quite clearly, we have some way to go.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Though there is some reason to be hopeful.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Just a few days ago, one Mr Koh Hock Neo contributed to The Straits Times Forum page, expressing his thanks to a Police Officer and a contractor on separate occasions, who had helped his sister who is hard of hearing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It is my strong belief that Singaporeans are a red-blooded, big-hearted people, sometimes, just a little shy.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Time and again, in moments of need, we have shown that we have so much room in our hearts for those amongst us with less and for those amongst us who are facing, quite frankly, different challenges in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Therefore, I call upon everyone – businesses, community partners, Members of this Chamber, everyone in Singapore society – to take interest and be the change, so that Singapore can truly be a shining beacon for the world in disability-inclusion!

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Through ComLink, we proactively reach out to and journey with these families to help them navigate life's challenges and seize opportunities, so that they can build a better future for themselves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our goal is for these families is to achieve the "3Ss": stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To do that, we place the family firmly at the centre of what we do, and we make sure that Government services and community resources are delivered in a comprehensive, convenient and coordinated manner.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Denise Phua asked about our progress for ComLink.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Community partners, including corporates, social enterprises and SSAs, have also contributed greatly to ComLink.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Other support such as monetary and in-kind donations have also poured in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have gone further upstream in extending our outreach by launching the ComLink Rental Scheme with HDB last year, as shared previously by Minister of State Faishal Ibrahim.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With the new scheme, families will be supported by ComLink officers once they apply for rental housing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With more proactive support, ComLink officers are better able to journey with families and provide them with support in other areas.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This holistic support earlier on in their journey will lead to better outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Allow me to share the story of Ms Fatin Nabilah, a single mother of three children who lives in a 2-room rental flat in Boon Lay.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Fatin works as an ad-hoc server at weddings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Jean Yi, an undergraduate at NTU, started befriending Fatin's family last May.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: When Jean Yi found out that Fatin was looking for jobs in the healthcare sector, she offered to recommend Fatin to a suitable job as her own elder sister is also in the healthcare sector.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: She opened up and began to trust Jean Yi.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Jean Yi's relationship with Fatin's family soon blossomed into one that is positive and trusting.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With Jean Yi's constant reassurance and encouragement, Fatin feels confident to achieve stability for her family.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At Jean Yi's suggestion, Fatin participated in the SGUnited Programme for Nursing and Healthcare and the "Daughters of Tomorrow" Confidence workshop.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Fatin's children also received academic support from ComLink programmes like the free tuition programme organised by Loving Heart Multi-Service Centre.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With support from the SSO, Jean Yi serves as Fatin's cheerleader, listening ear and a mentor to the little ones.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Befrienders like Jean Yi play a key role in ComLink.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Indeed, we are looking for people who are empathetic, open-minded and most important of all, passionate about journeying with ComLink families towards their goals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We welcome all who fit the bill to step forward as ComLink befrienders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To complement community efforts, we have been strengthening Government services delivery.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As Deputy Prime Minister Wong mentioned in his Budget Speech, we are working with relevant agencies to further integrate services that support ComLink families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked about our plans to achieve this.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Families living in rental flats often run pillar to post, filling out multiple forms, repeating their stories and struggles at different offices to receive all the help they need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Each family will be assigned to ComLink befrienders who will be their consistent touchpoint.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our intent is to scale and benefit more families this way in other ComLink communities.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Ms Denise Phua also asked about challenges in implementing ComLink.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Apart from the effort involved in integrating service delivery across agencies, the work on the ground is high-touch and we need more befrienders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Empathy, the human touch and personal connection are crucial as we reach out to ComLink families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To be sure, we also need families to be open and receptive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Not all families may immediately see the need for befriending or to work on an action plan.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Beyond ComLink, we have other avenues of support for lower-income families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Assoc Prof Jamus Lim and Mr Leon Perera made various suggestions to improve support for low-income families such as reducing the need for documentation and enhancing the financial assistance schemes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On the three specific groups that Mr Leon Perera referenced, today, they can already walk into the SSO, and the SSO officers will be able to follow up with each of them on their cases.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Also, referral protocols are already in place, including between MHA, MINDEF and MSF.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Over the past few years, we have been putting in place various arrangements, including system links, with other agencies to reduce the documentation required of ComCare applicants.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are also streamlining application processes to make it easier for applicants to seek support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is also another example of providing integrated support in a family-centric manner that Ms Joan Pereira also talked about.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is only one example of how we are starting off the process of making different processes more streamlined, starting with ComCare.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Today, there are already financial assistance schemes that cover both education expenses as well as subsidies and grants for childcare, kindergarten and student care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For students who require more dedicated help in coping with their studies, our schools run various programmes to ensure that these students receive adequate additional learning support and guidance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Self-help groups and other community partners also provide support, such as academic help for students from lower-income families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We regularly review the adequacy of our assistance schemes for the lower income.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We introduced temporary measures to provide ComCare assistance for a longer duration and at a higher quantum during the pandemic and increased assistance for ComCare schemes last August.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will continue to monitor the adequacy of our schemes and make necessary adjustments where appropriate.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Supporting lower-income families to help them achieve stability, self-reliance and social mobility must be a whole-of-society effort.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Within the public sector, we will step up our efforts to coordinate and synergise our efforts across agency boundaries, with support centred on the family.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will enhance training for our frontline officers, including those at our SSOs, to equip them with the knowledge and skills that they need to work effectively in this new paradigm of social service delivery.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But we also need the community, social service agencies, corporates, academics and volunteers, to join hands with us, so that we can build a strong and cohesive Singapore for all.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In Mandarin):   Our vision for Singapore is to be a caring and inclusive society, much like how it was in the "kampung" days.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Every family faces different problems and challenges in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It is not difficult to imagine that the challenges faced by families with disabilities are even more different from those faced by other families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SG Enable will also be setting up the first EBH this year in Jurong West, in collaboration with social service partners and businesses.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This will bring more inclusive employment opportunities closer to where PwDs live.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This collaboration with businesses will drive inclusive hiring with job redesign and technology.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Apart from families with PwDs, another group that we must support is our lower-income families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These families often face unique and complex challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: However, like families with PwDs, we must provide coordinated, convenient and comprehensive support and services that are tailored to the circumstances and considerations of each family.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I am heartened to see that many families who have benefited from ComLink are working hard to give themselves, their children and their families a better future.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Some families want a stable job, some want to save enough for their children's education, while some want to own a house one day.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Regardless of their aspirations and goals, we are committed to work with these families and provide them with the support and assistance they need.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As we move towards the future, we must support each other so that no one gets left behind in the long run.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: (In English): Sir, I would like to conclude by sharing a story.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Recently, I met a 10-year-old girl, Ratu, at a flea market in Lengkok Bahru.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Intrigued by a bucket of cute "stuff" that she was holding, I asked her what she was doing. "I'm selling these handphone charms, 50 cents a scoop!" was her spirited reply.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And with that, I was a customer; I was sold.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: You can see this small little thing here?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This was exactly what I observed in Lengkok Bahru.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Families connected to one another, not by blood, but by their common motivation to help one another out in taking on life's challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And there are the big-hearted "cheerleaders" who have consistently journeyed with these families.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mr Chairman, just three clarifications – one each for the Minister, Minister of State and Senior Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: First, to Minister of State Sun Xueling, I think we are all cheered by the fact that with the revision in salaries and appreciation for preschool educators, we have seen an increase in the number entering this career.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: But for infant care teachers, I am quite sure many of us are experiencing that there is a long waitlist.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: There, certainly, is a long waitlist at the preschool centres in my constituency.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Therefore, my first clarification is, what can we do to increase the supply of infant care teachers, so that it will help to shorten the queues for them?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We are heartened by the top-up of $300 million into the ComCare Endowment Fund.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: We know that the cost of living has gone up.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: My simple question is, on the review of both ComCare and Public Assistance scheme, when is this due, because for all those who are receiving these, the last year, in particular, has been quite hard on them.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: And my third clarification is for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I refer to a suggestion by Mr Leon Perera where he suggested that we could dispense for SSOs to probably dispense or simplify the need to verify certain documents.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: My own take is that we need to be cautious about this.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: I would rather say and hope that, instead, SSOs be empowered more to exercise greater flexibility to work within the guidelines and yet, exercise flexibility on a case-by-case basis as they evaluate each of these ComCare applicants.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
