text: We all recognise that, indeed, we do have a shortage of manpower in the early childhood industry.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Member is right that it is in the areas of infant care educators, infant care carers, that we do face an acute shortage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, ECDA has embarked on a three-pronged approach.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I have mentioned reviewing of their working conditions, ensuring competitive salaries and also ensuring that they have good skills development and that there is career progression for them.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Over and above these three areas, ECDA is also working with AOPs and other preschool operators to step up recruitment through online means as well as through job fairs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We are also working with AOPs, where possible, for them to consider diverting their manpower internally so that there is good deployment between infant care and childcare where they are operating in the same premises.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Over and above that, as I have mentioned in my main speech, we are working with the AOPs to actively reach out to both local and foreign sources of manpower.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We definitely hope that we can encourage more people to consider joining the early childhood education industry.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I have mentioned that we are tapping on community networks and these community networks are very wide.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It will include People's Association (PA), Daughters Of Tomorrow and also "Women at Work" by MENDAKI.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, through these combined efforts, we hope to be able to encourage more to join the early childhood education industry.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But having said that, the income eligibility criteria are not hard thresholds because the SSOs can assess holistically the family, their needs, because if their basic needs cannot be met, no matter what their income is presented to be, the SSOs do have the discretion to support them.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, we do have flexibility to exercise on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Chairman, I thank the Member for his suggestion and his comment.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And I just want to go on to add – and also to add to Minister Masagos' point – about the fact that the SSO general managers and staff do have some discretion, especially when giving out quick and immediate support.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Oftentimes, we get feedback that SSO applications take about four to six weeks to get approved.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: That is for a large percentage of all cases that come in.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But beyond that, the general managers do have some discretionary funds within each SSO for them to take some quick actions as well.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I appreciate the points made by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: That is in relation to the suggestions I made about significantly enhancing the ComCare grant quantums in line with minimum income standard research, extending the runway perhaps to a year and making the application process less onerous in terms of interviewing family members and documents and so on.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: My clarification would be: would the Ministry be open to experimentation, doing a pilot to see if we do these things and make significant changes, whether the net benefits will outweigh the risk or the downside in terms of reducing that bandwidth tax, reducing the stress, enabling that trampoline effect where families are able to plan ahead and plan a turnaround in their life?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And also, just improving the outcomes of their children as they go through this life that they have to go through, which they did not choose to go through.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I think Assoc Prof Jamus Lim made some similar suggestions as well.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Chairman, I thank the Member for his additional suggestions.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think there were a couple of things that were said; well, quite a number of things were said.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think, first of all, it is the reference to the minimum income study.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think that has been covered in the last COS and addressed by Minister Masagos.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I will not go into it in great detail.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think our position on that has been clear; there have been previous press releases by the Ministry of Finance, as well with regard to that study.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To two other points that the Member made regarding the application process.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think the Member also was nodding away when I was talking about SupportGoWhere and ComCare applications being made easy through SupportGoWhere.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: That is just the start of our entire journey.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We are on the cusp of change in the social service delivery landscape, if I could put it that way.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And I think ComCare being on SupportGoWhere is just one of the starting points for us in revolutionising the delivery of social services.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, that is one part of the thing about the ease of application for social service applications.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Of course, this is more operational than policy that they have one point of contact for all the different services, have the befriender and the ComLink engagement officer (CEO) working together to make sure that what is presented in terms of an action plan to each family is coherent, it is not obfuscating to the family, it is not confusing to the family.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: That is only the start of what we are looking at.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But essentially, a part of ComLink's DNA is about daring to do new things policy-wise as well.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think some of these moves would be gradually revealed as some of the details are being worked out.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I urge the Member to watch the space for announcements related to ComLink.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I wish to commend MSF for taking on this very bold experiment.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I feel like ComLink is almost undertaking a massive endeavour that is similar to what SSAs might do.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: So, my question is, does the ComLink programme have headcounts within MSF that play a dedicated volunteer management role?

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Depending on the answer, I might ask further.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Depending on your answer, you may get more questions.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think the short answer is there is never enough manpower.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But the longer answer is that behind each befriender, we are not leaving the befriender to do his or her job alone.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In my speech, I said the befriender will put things together almost like a character from Mission Impossible, harnessing things in the coherent plan for the family, having great knowledge of the different schemes and programmes, both on the Government's side of the house and the community's side of the house, and present a coherent plan to the family.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: He or she is supported by a CEO, who is a staff of the SSO.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, the short answer and the longer answer is, yes, the befrienders are supported by these so-called professionals at the SSO, behind the scenes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: There is a certain type that we look for in a befriender.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And Ms Carrie Tan, being in this sector for a long time, would know that we want those who are big-hearted, red-blooded and have a big heart for ComLink families to be able to journey with them for the long haul.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Because we are not talking about volunteering for ad hoc occasions, we are talking about going at it for months and sometimes, perhaps, even for a couple of years, at least, with each family, understanding them in depth and then proposing and perhaps, nudging and working through with these families – as equals, of course – on the situations that they are in.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, I feel that the bar for befrienders is also high.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: If anything else, I would really make a clarion call for more to step up to be befrienders.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: And I thank the Member for highlighting this issue on manpower as well.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I will come back to you, Ms Tan.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: My question is also for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Thirdly, how else can the business sector help so that PwDs have a higher chance to stay engaged?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Chair, I thank the Member for her clarification.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think she would agree with me that the sheltered workshops' environment is very much suitable and amenable to PwIDs, not so much for persons with autism.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Alongside this, what is happening behind the scenes is also the fact that we are trying to review some of the service models to see how we can change up the way sheltered workshops are being organised: what they can do or what they cannot do or what they could do in the future.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, we are trying to future-proof or move the sheltered workshop model into a more advanced stage.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We welcome corporates to have a conversation with us because it is only by understanding where business needs are, understanding where persons with disabilities' needs as well as caregivers' needs are and forming these few pieces together and that overlap in the Venn diagram – that is the sweet spot that we want to land.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think that is exactly the harder piece of work that we are trying to work at behind the scenes right now.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, I do not have a ready answer, but I thank the Member for shining the light on this part of work that we are doing.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I have no doubt that the befrienders are currently supported by very technically sound and competent MSF officers.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: But I think it kind of misses the point, because volunteer management requires someone with a very wide variety of skillsets, including being a cheerleader, a peer support facilitator for the volunteers, strong in communications so that they can continuously share uplifting stories, help to boost their morale, listen to them, sometimes be an Aunt Agony, because befrienders themselves could be impacted by the stories that they see.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: I do not think that this is a role that can be underestimated.

speaker: Ms Carrie Tan
text: Hence, I think it is critically important, especially if we want to ramp up the number of volunteer befrienders, that we have people with the right background experience and expertise to actually do this well for ComLink to be able to be implemented well.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think my mobile phone charm is not working very well.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, to the point that the Member raised, I fully agree with her that a wide range of skillsets are needed.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Again, I go back to my centre of gravity earlier about the roles of the befriender vis-à-vis the role of the CEO.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Before the CEO comes to where he or she is in the SSO, I am sure he or she goes through a rigorous set of training under the ambit of the SSO before he or she gets to where he or she is serving.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But I just want to expand a little bit more about what the befrienders go through.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: To me, the befriender is the first touchpoint for our ComLink families.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: On ComLink, to be more effective, I think we need to have more information sharing.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: Can I ask the Senior Parliamentary Secretary if this is being done now and if so, how can we help our SSOs so that it is facilitated across all the various agencies and it will be more helpful in their job?

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: We do involve the other visceral parts of the ecosystem as well.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: For instance, the volunteer centres under the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth's (MCCY's) SG Cares.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In terms of how we reach out to each Member, we also give regular updates by email.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: Feel free to approach me as well because I am in charge of the ComLink that is part of Henderson-Dawson.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, feel free to reach out for updates on the information.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: But where there are programmes and initiatives that you think are worthy of propagating, not just across the ComLink towns, but they can be something that can be shared across towns.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: That is put on a list that is shared with all ComLink Committees.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: In that sense, information sharing has been ongoing.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: It has been very much behind the scenes.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: I think we can do more to bring it forward to all who are involved on the ground.

speaker: The Chairman
text: If not, Mr Seah, do you wish to withdraw your cut?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Mr Chairman, it has been a long week.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: It is Friday and it is a quarter past eight.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: First, on behalf of all of us who raised cuts at this COS debate for Head I, I would like to thank Minister Masagos, Minister of State Sun Xueling and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua for their comprehensive and considered replies to all our questions.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: Likewise, I think I speak for all to express our sincere appreciation to all those in the social service sector for their big hearts, for their care, for the compassion and for their patience as we all journey together to make Singapore a more caring, a more inclusive and a more giving community.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
text: With that, Sir, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
